question: Which of the following revolutionary books was authored by Veer Savarkar in 1923, whose birth anniversary was commemorated on 28th May 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindutva: Who is a Hindu?**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **Hindutva: Who is a Hindu?** was authored by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** (popularly known as **Veer Savarkar**) and was published in **1923**.
 
• The book was written while **Savarkar** was imprisoned in **Ratnagiri** jail and under internment; it was initially published under the pseudonym **'A Maratha'** to avoid British censorship.
 
• In this work, **Savarkar** systematically defined the concept of **Hindutva** as an all-encompassing political and cultural identity, distinct from the religious rituals of **Hinduism**.
 
• **Savarkar's** birth anniversary falls on **28th May**; the year **2025** commemorates his **142nd birth anniversary**, as he was born in **1883** in the village of **Bhagur**, **Nashik** district, **Maharashtra**.
 
• The core thesis of the book posits that a **Hindu** is anyone who considers **India** (Bharatvarsha) as their **Pitribhu** (Fatherland) and **Punyabhu** (Holy land). ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **My Experiments with Truth:**
 
 
• This is the autobiography of **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi** (Mahatma Gandhi).
 
• It was originally written in **Gujarati** and published as a series in his journal **Navjivan** between **1925** and **1929**.
 
• The book covers **Gandhi's** life from his childhood in **Porbandar** to the year **1921**, focusing on his spiritual and moral development.
 
 
 
• **The Discovery of India:**
 
 
• Written by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first **Prime Minister** of India.
 
• It was written during his imprisonment at **Ahmednagar Fort** between **1942** and **1945** following the **Quit India Movement**.
 
• The book provides a comprehensive analysis of Indian history, philosophy, and culture from the **Indus Valley Civilization** to the British **Raj**.
 
 
 
• **India Wins Freedom:**
 
 
• This is an autobiographical account by **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress** and India's first **Education Minister**.
 
• The book offers an insider's view of the **Indian Independence** movement, the **Partition of India**, and **Azad's** personal views on the political leaders of that era.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Revolutionary Contributions:** **Veer Savarkar** founded the secret society **Abhinav Bharat Society** in **1904** to promote armed rebellion against British rule.
 
• **1857 War of Independence:** He authored another famous book, **The Indian War of Independence 1857**, in which he was among the first to describe the **1857** uprising as the **"First War of Independence"** rather than a mere sepoy mutiny.
 
• **Cellular Jail:** For his revolutionary activities, he was sentenced to two life terms (50 years) and sent to the **Cellular Jail** (Kala Pani) in the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** in **1911**.
 
• **Political Leadership:** He served as the **President** of the **Hindu Mahasabha** from **1937** to **1943**, where he advocated for the rights of the Hindu community and a militarized **India**.
